topics.topic: Whether valid progress photo updates always persist and audit, or can be rolled back as replays, and how replay is identified
questions: Must every valid update write, append the PHOTO_UPDATE audit, and commit, or is there an update replay path that rolls back; if a replay path exists, what defines it?

quotes: update_progress_photo: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST validate optional section project scope, change only caption/section/client_visible/updated_at/updated_by, and append AuditAction.PHOTO_UPDATE atomically without changing file_ref, progress, or finance.

update_progress_photo: [DEPENDENCY_BOUNDARY] MUST open exactly one transaction, read the photo only through tx.progress_photos().get_progress_photo with photo_id, resolve a supplied section only through tx.project_sections().get_project_section with context.project_id inside that same transaction, write only through tx.progress_photos().update_progress_photo, append the audit only through tx.audit(), and on success commit exactly once (a replay or a validation failure closes it by rollback instead); it MUST NOT call validate_project_section, open a second transaction while its own is active, or use a legacy transaction-level photo or project-section method.

update_progress_photo: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] MUST append exactly one AuditAction.PHOTO_UPDATE success audit through tx.audit() with entity_kind PROGRESS_PHOTO, entity_id equal to the canonical string of the updated photo_id, and reason_code None; a non-null reason_code on a success audit is rejected by the audit writer and MUST NOT be supplied.
judgement.divergence: One careful implementer treats every valid update, including one whose requested values equal the stored values, as a write that appends PHOTO_UPDATE and commits; another classifies some valid update as a replay and rolls it back without writing or auditing, but the texts never define the replay identity or comparison. The owner and audit consumers notice the differing persisted update metadata and audit history, and the caller can notice the returned updated_at.
judgement.why: The update requirements mention a replay rollback path but neither define how an update becomes a replay nor reconcile that path with the unconditional write-and-audit obligations.

topics.topic: Whether transport logging must strip query/fragment from canonical_path or write it whole unchanged
questions: If _canonical_path preserves a query string, _transport_log_record cannot both write canonical_path whole exactly as received and produce a path field without a query string; which requirement must change?

How can the log contain the canonical path without a query string when _canonical_path must preserve query and fragment and _transport_log_record must write its canonical_path argument whole and unchanged; which requirement must change?
When canonical_path contains a query string, must it be removed from the path field, or must canonical_path be written whole exactly as received?

quotes: It MUST NOT strip the segment more than once, strip a longer prefix, alter query or fragment, or treat a path that merely begins with the letters api as prefixed.

_transport_log_record: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST build one line of exactly four labelled fields in this order and shape, so an operator log parser does not change between builds: 'rid=<request id> method=<method> path=<canonical path without query string> status=<status>'.
The line is bounded in its fields, not in its length: canonical_path is written whole, exactly as received, and MUST NOT be truncated, shortened or escaped.
judgement.why: The canonical path must preserve a query or fragment, while the log simultaneously must omit the query string and write that path whole exactly as received.

quotes: _transport_log_record: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST build one line of exactly four labelled fields in this order and shape, so an operator log parser does not change between builds: 'rid=<request id> method=<method> path=<canonical path without query string> status=<status>'.
The line is bounded in its fields, not in its length: canonical_path is written whole, exactly as received, and MUST NOT be truncated, shortened or escaped.
judgement.why: A canonical path containing a line break cannot be written whole and unescaped while the resulting record remains one line, and field-like path text can add apparent labelled fields despite the exactly-four-field requirement.
